visualReview.notes: All13 current portable views actually inspected: lit overview, four turntables, full frontal/oblique plan and eight detail views. True niche depth, connected inner cornice, layered rock, opaque still-water interpretation and dry stairs reviewed. Rear is the explicitly bounded backing facade, not a modeled full palace. Six individually inspected local originals (2006–2022) plus28 contact thumbnails constrain the immediate present exterior. Native facade/site/water traces, four giant columns, deep coffered triumphal niche and four inner columns/continuous curved entablature, two allegory niches, three shutter-window bays per wing, four attic figures and papal shield/tiara/winged figures are retained. Static posed human/horse anatomy is baked from the public figures kernel then given photo-directed drapery, Oceanus forward leg/beard/shell chariot, different rearing horse poses, marine tails and seated trumpet figures. These are intentionally faceted medium-fi sculpture interpretations; facial carving, fingers, inscriptions and exact stone relief are generalized. Rough ledges and three curved ribbed spill drops are separate from the mapped main basin and nine dry amphitheatre steps. No photographic pixels copied.

mediumFiReview.notes: All25 current original-field context images actually inspected: street/block/skyline, noon/late, economy/high, silhouette, eight details and four explicit LOD transitions. Current exact asset/runtime/LOD hashes checked in every frame. Nine actual downward ray probes per frame find no rendered ground over the physical opening; both original terrain and distant backdrop are cut, original source coordinates unchanged. Corrected review fixture bakes the horizontal backdrop orientation into its geometry so the X/Z cutout is meaningful. Basin and dry steps remain visible. Synthetic neighboring houses are context only; geographic placement separately checked.

fidelityReview.notes: The cleared RoyFokker night exterior confirms the central giant arch, paired columns, lateral statue niches and layered rocky water basins. Current pale architectural composition and simplified statues preserve the recognizable hierarchy. Side palace fabric, anatomy, rock detail and precise hydraulic elements remain approximate; night lighting is not baked into materials. Accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi exterior scope. No reference pixels are embedded. Previously used attribution/private imagery is excluded from this current review.

limitations: Native map geometry is quantized and low-zoom; precise sculpted rock placement and facade heights are photographic interpretations, not a construction survey.
Native whole-fountain envelope differs from actual water edge. Preserve both; do not fill the whole envelope with water.
Mapped Palazzo Poli has rear courts and wings; asset scope covers fountain facade and immediate backing thickness, not complete palace or its interior.
Statues, arms, horses, shell chariot and papal crest must retain interpreted recognizable silhouettes; no exact facial/inscription/art-conservation reproduction.
Native map preparation establishes location and signed axes; geometry, independent terrain and actual visual/placement acceptance must be separately verified before any completion annotation.

Facade width49.69m follows mapped line;26.3m reported overall height is a non-survey visual control. Individual cornices, column dimensions, water/step levels, rock positions and statue poses are photographic estimates. Sculptures retain restrained silhouettes, not exact faces, muscle/finger/fabric detail or copied reliefs/inscriptions.

Immediate4.2m backing facade is a bounded wall volume, not the complete Palazzo Poli. No interior, water simulation, fountain plumbing or navigable collision claim. Waterfall strips are static pale geometric surfaces.

Original Terrarium pixels may oversample much coarser composite source data;1m sampling does not imply survey accuracy. Provider-relative vertical reference only; default coarse host terrain compatibility not certified.

Fine sculpture and rock surfaces are conservative faceted interpretations from photographs, not a sculptural survey or exact replica. Water is an opaque static surface; no real fluid simulation or submerged bathymetry.
Bounded immediate Palazzo Poli fountain facade only; full palace and neighboring city remain separate supporting context.
